newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees jobless rising as state firms close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees jobless rising as state firms close.

text.p: The number of jobless in Bulgaria is expected to rise by end-year because of the planned closure of loss-making state enterprises, National Labour Exchange chairman Dimitrov told reporters.
The socialist government, in a bid to win crucial funding from international lending institutions, has pledged to close down 64 debt-ridden state firms employing up to 40,000 people.
"Latest figures show that some 7,600 people have lost their jobs due to the liquidation of state firms so far," Dimitrov said.
The number of people seeking work by year-end depended on what was done with the firms on the closure list, he said.
Some state firms initially slated for liquidation, such as the second largest oil refinery, Plama,were actually privatised.

Cash-strapped Bulgaria is expected to speed up liquidation of loss-makers after the International Monetary Fund postponed the second tranche of a loan earlier this month until the cabinet completes the closures, analysts said.
The NLE earlier reported August unemployment was stable at 396,155 or 10.4 percent of the workforce, unchanged from July and down from 10.7 percent a year earlier. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
